newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 27.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- South and North Korean Red Cross delegations signed an agreement in Beijing on direct delivery of aid between the two countries, promising 50,000 tonnes of food to the impoverished North by the end of July.
- Former Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung, an advisor of the ruling New Korea Party, announced that he would seek the ruling party's presidential nomination.

- President Kim Young-sam is once again considering addressing the issue of his 1992 campaign funds. He is expected to hold a luncheon meeting with nine presidential hopefuls from his ruling New Korea Party.

- Twenty-nine member countries of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, including Korea, have taken an important step in making it a crime to bribe foreign officals as they agreed on Monday to put into effect an anti-bribery treaty by next April.
- U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said in a meeting in Paris with Korean Trade and Energy minister Lim Chang-yeul that he will push visa waivers for Korean businessmen and tourists.
